title: Largest superpositions: porphyrins (2019) and Na clusters (2026)

checks.name: record overlap left after the flight, porphyrin 26.8 kDa (Fein 2019) (worst of N2/H2)
checks.note: ionization energy not reported; 7 eV assumed (typical large organic)

checks.name: thermal-photon scattering exponent, porphyrin 26.8 kDa (Fein 2019)
checks.note: far below threshold: 300 K photons (~10 um) cannot resolve ~100 nm

checks.name: record overlap left after the flight, Na cluster 172 kDa (Pedalino 2026) (worst of N2/H2)
checks.note: first ionization threshold 2.53 eV from the paper

checks.name: thermal-photon scattering exponent, Na cluster 172 kDa (Pedalino 2026)
checks.note: far below threshold: 300 K photons (~10 um) cannot resolve ~100 nm

notes: Both superpositions survive because the vacuum makes collisions rare and room-temperature photons are far too long to resolve the path separation. The domain here is the full path separation, held for the whole flight.
